Khoirul Anwar (born 24 February 1978) is an Indonesian scientist and educator recognized for his significant contributions to wireless communication technology, particularly 4G LTE standards. He is an associate professor at Telkom University and serves as the Director of the Center for Advanced Wireless Technologies (AdWiTech).
Academic and technical contributions
Anwar's primary technical achievement is the invention of the double Fast Fourier Transform (Two-FFT) technique. This method enhances data transmission efficiency in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems. His work has been integrated into international technical standards, specifically ITU-R S.1878 and ITU-R S.2173 by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
In 2025, Anwar was noted for his leadership in global forums regarding the implementation of 6G technology, focusing on quantum-secure communications and high-speed data rates.
Early life and education
Anwar was born into a modest farming family in Kediri Regency. His upbringing as a livestock grass collector (ngarit) is frequently highlighted in national biographies as a foundational period of his discipline. He graduated from the Bandung Institute of Technology (ITB) in 2000 and obtained his Doctorate from the Nara Institute of Science and Technology (NAIST) in Japan in 2008.
Awards and recognition
* IEEE Best Student Paper Award (2006)
* Achmad Bakrie Award (2014)
* Habibie Award (2014)
